blocks.title: Risk Treatment, Reporting, and Business Impact Analysis comparison
Risk Treatment, Reporting, and Business Impact Analysis exam shortcuts
items: Buy insurance → TRANSFER
Transfer shifts some consequences to another party.
Example: Cyber insurance covers defined incident costs.
Risk is within approved limits and no new control is added → ACCEPT
Acceptance means knowingly living with the risk.
Example: Management documents residual risk.
Stop the risky activity entirely → AVOID
Avoidance removes the source of the risk.
Example: Retire an unsupported internet-facing system.
Add a control to lower probability or damage → MITIGATE
Mitigation reduces likelihood or impact.
Example: Add MFA to reduce account-compromise risk.
How quickly must service return? → RTO
RTO is time to restoration.
Example: Payroll system must return within four hours.
How much recent data may be lost? → RPO
RPO is acceptable data-loss window.
Example: 15-minute RPO requires frequent replication or backups.
Average time to fix failure → MTTR
MTTR measures repair or restoration time.
Example: Average outage repair takes two hours.
Average time between failures → MTBF
MTBF measures reliability.
Example: Device averages 5,000 operating hours between failures.
blocks.example: Watch for formula clues, recovery-time wording, and the difference between broad risk appetite and specific risk tolerance.

questions.q: A company buys cyber insurance to cover certain incident costs. Which risk strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Risk transfer shifts some consequences to another party, such as an insurer.

questions.q: Management documents a low residual risk and chooses not to implement additional controls. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Acceptance means knowingly living with the risk within approved limits.

questions.q: A company retires an unsupported internet-facing application because the risk is too high. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Avoidance eliminates the risky activity or condition.

questions.q: A company adds MFA to reduce account-compromise risk. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Mitigation reduces likelihood or impact by adding controls.

questions.q: A legacy system receives formal approval to be excluded from a specific security requirement. What is this?
questions.explanation: An exemption formally excludes a system or situation from a requirement.

questions.q: A temporary deviation from a patching requirement is approved until the next maintenance window. What is this?
questions.explanation: An exception is an approved temporary or specific deviation.

questions.q: A payroll system must be restored within four hours after an outage. What does four hours represent?
questions.explanation: RTO is the targeted maximum time to restore a service or process.

questions.q: A database may lose no more than 15 minutes of data after a disruption. What does 15 minutes represent?
questions.explanation: RPO is the maximum acceptable data-loss window measured in time.

questions.q: A device takes an average of two hours to repair after failure. Which metric is this?
questions.explanation: MTTR measures average repair or restoration time.

questions.q: A server averages 5,000 operating hours between failures. Which metric is this?
questions.explanation: MTBF measures average operating time between failures.

questions.q: An organization analyzes which business processes are most critical and the impact of downtime. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: A BIA identifies critical business functions and the impact of disruption.
